findings.title: Capacity tariff: single-zone solver stalls on the top-k peak plateau, plans 1-4 SEK/day dearer than needed
findings.claim: With the golden capacity_tariff_15min settings the single-zone plan is beaten on its own objective at comfort parity in 15 of 16 winter_cold price x DHW cells (mean 1.26 SEK per solve excluding the negative-price cell, 2.19 % of objective, 3.28 % of the daily bill; 58.29 SEK on summer_negative/winter_cold/nodhw), and production's answer has |projected gradient| 0.03-20 SEK/kW against PGTOL 1e-5 in 16/16 cells.
findings.mechanism: tariff.peak_cost sums the top-k (peak_count=3) window excesses, so a plan with more than k metering windows tied at the peak is a plateau on which the 2-point gradient sees only k windows; the per-iteration reduction is tiny relative to the objective and L-BFGS-B's ftol=1e-6 FACTR test fires at a non-stationary point. A same-settings restart recovers 0.66-0.92 SEK in 7/16 cells; ftol=1e-9 removes the restart gap entirely; peak_count=16 collapses the 58 SEK cell to 0.13 SEK.

evidence.value: cells_with_gap_sz=15 of 16; mean_energy_gap_pct_bill_sz=2.517; mean gap 1.255 SEK with the 58.285 SEK cell dropped; restart_improves_sz=7; pg_above_pgtol_sz=16; mean_restart_gap_sek_sz=0.1661
evidence.machine: Apple M1 8-core 8 GB, macOS 25.6, python 3.13.1, numpy 2.5.2, scipy 1.18.1, OpenBLAS pinned to 1 thread
evidence.contention_note: fan-out: ten other auditors on the box, load1 1.5-70 during the day; counts and SEK gaps on the production objective are contention-immune
evidence.tolerance: counts exact; SEK gaps +/-1e-3 (L-BFGS-B is deterministic on this build)

findings.title: Two-zone solves stop on FACTR at non-stationary points; a restart recovers up to 2.16 SEK/day (masked by re-planning)
findings.claim: On the 24 h price x weather grid, re-submitting production's answer to the identical L-BFGS-B call improves the two-zone plan by more than 1e-3 SEK in 15/80 cells (mean 0.052 SEK; winter_narrow/winter_cold/tz/dhw 2.163 SEK = 1.75 % of a 123.4 SEK bill, winter_typical/winter_cold/tz/dhw 0.954 SEK = 1.4 % of 69.0 SEK); production's answer has |projected gradient| > PGTOL in 64/80 two-zone cells and the restart gap vanishes at flat prices (max 0.0011 SEK).
findings.mechanism: L-BFGS-B's relative-reduction stop (ftol=1e-6) fires on a stalled iteration of the two-zone objective when the price signal creates ill-conditioned basins; a fresh curvature memory from the same point continues to descend. The seed-found part of the whole-race gap (49/80 cells, mean 0.109 SEK) survives flat prices (0.155 SEK) and is non-convexity, not price optimality.

findings.title: Small buffer tank with a mixing valve: cap-tightened re-solve stops at a kink, 3.5-4.2 SEK/day dearer, floor breached
findings.claim: With the golden valve_storage_small_tank config (35 L buffer, manual valve, tank at 32 C) swept over the 8 price profiles (two-zone, no DHW, winter_cold), production's plan is beaten at comfort parity in 5/8 cells, mean 1.13 SEK per solve (4.4 % of the energy bill), max 4.19 SEK (winter_moderate) and 3.47 SEK on winter_typical where production's own plan breaches the comfort floor by 0.112 K-steps while the bang-bang challenger breaches 0.000; |projected gradient| at production's answer is 2 to 1.1e4 SEK/kW in 8/8 cells.
findings.mechanism: The _tighten_buffer_caps loop in optimize lowers per-step power caps where the tank clamp refused heat and re-solves from the same three starts; the clamp deletes heat so the objective is kinked at the cap, production's starts descend onto the kink and the FACTR test fires there (winter_typical: 3 multi-start calls, pg 131 at the adopted one).

evidence.value: cells_with_gap_tz=5 of 8; mean_gap_sek_tz=1.1333; max_gap_sek_tz=4.1884; mean_energy_gap_pct_bill_tz=4.396; pg_above_pgtol_tz=8; winter_typical gap 3.4708 SEK (3.90 %) with production under=0.1119 K-steps vs challenger 0.0000 (race_scenarios.py --only small_tank --verbose)
